subject: Medilens Dedicated sizing: surge resilience & headroom plan
messages:
From: Kate Morgan <kate@medilens.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: salesops@medilens.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial notes on Dedicated sizing

Thanks for the call earlier — attaching the rough traffic sketch we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Peak traffic window: 09:00–11:00 PT weekdays, sustained for 90 minutes, with occasional spikes lasting up to 6 minutes.
- Typical request: user prompt → 800–1,200 tokens in, expected output ~350–900 tokens.
- Concurrency target: we expect 180 concurrent active sessions during peak (concurrent inferences waiting on generation).
- SLO target for 95th pctl latency: < 600ms for streaming-friendly UX; fallback acceptable up to 1.5s for degraded mode.

We want a Dedicated pool with predictable cost and fast failover to hosted variants during maintenance. Please confirm what headroom you recommend and any quantization/latency tradeoffs you see.

Thanks,
Kate
VP Product, MediLens

(Attachment: medilens-traffic-sketch.pdf)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Morgan <kate@medilens.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial notes on Dedicated sizing

Kate — thanks, this is perfect context. Quick readout from our side after sketching an initial tokens/sec model (see attached spreadsheet):

Summary bullets:
- Estimated tokens/sec (sustained, peak window): 17k–22k tokens/sec across the fleet assuming behavior above (median prompt+resp ~1,000 tokens).
- Target SLO mapping: with fp16 single-GPU runs on A100-like instances, we estimate ~3.5–4.5k tokens/sec per GPU for this model family (depending on seq length). That implies a baseline of 5–6 GPUs for meet-minimum, 8 GPUs to hit SLO with 20% headroom.
- Quantized 4bit/8bit profiles reduce GPU footprint (~1.8–2.5x tokens/sec per GPU improvement) but add ~10–18% variability on tail latency; recommend Q4+fp16 hybrid for latency-sensitive paths.
- Recommended safe commit: Dedicated pool sized for 8 GPUs + 2 GPU burst buffer (spare nodes for fast failover) with automatic fallback routing to hosted instances on overload.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you share a one-week sample of request timestamps (anonymized) so we can simulate burst shapes?
2) If you need stricter 99th pctl latency, we should plan for +30% capacity or enforce shorter max output lengths.
3) I'll loop in Prio for the runbook and Ben for pricing carve-out.

Sending the model workbook and an early runbook draft.

—Logan
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Attachments: medilens-tps-model.xlsx, dedicated-runbook-v1.pdf)

Looping in pricing ops + a quick commercial note:

- If we size the Dedicated commit at 8 GPUs with 2 spare for burst (10 committed), monthly committed fee aligns to the DL-500 Tier; estimate attached "commit-costs" sheet in the workbook.
- We can offer a 10% commit credit for a 12-month term and a one-time migration credit to cover the initial performance tuning.
- DocuSign/MAP: please confirm the top-line (desired commit GPUs and term length) and we'll push a draft MAP that includes 30-day SLA exceptions for maintenance windows.

Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Kate — thanks, confirmed for 09:30 PT tomorrow (calendar invite sent). Quick pre-read summary we'll walk through on the call (so you can validate during the session):

Walkthrough agenda (15–30m):
- Walk the tokens/sec model from the workbook: assumptions (median seq, generation length, early stop rate).
- SLO sensitivity table: baseline (8 GPUs + 2 burst), padded (+30% = 11 GPUs), and quantized hybrid option (6 GPUs + 2 burst) with expected 99th pctl ranges.
- Failover & routing: how we route excess to hosted API, cold-start mitigation for warm caches, and KV-prefix caching recommendations to reduce token load by ~12–18%.
- Ops playbook: detection thresholds, automated scaling triggers, and standby burst activation timeline.

Deliverables we will update after the session:
1) final dedicated sizing recommendation with cost delta (8 vs 11 GPU commit).
2) updated MAP including migration credit and quarterly optimization checkpoint language.
3) runbook edits reflecting your sample logs and spike shape.

We're attaching the draft Mutual Action Plan for review — please flag any legal/commercial items you want pulled into the DocuSign draft.

See you tomorrow.
